image_description: A dorsal view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a surface. The organism has an elongated oval shape with a distinct border. The central area features eight overlapping, transverse calcareous plates (valves) that are greyish-green with vertical striations. These plates are surrounded by a thick, textured, brownish girdle (mantle) that appears granular or spiny. There are no visible eyes, tentacles, or limbs.
